issues.problem:
Both ranks still order by the raw height p.cy (ranked line 551 `{ -v, p.cy, abs(qx), ... }`, measureRanked line 602 `{ -p.volume, p.cy, ... }`). Take two twin parts with the same volume and height whose heights differ only in the last bit. A whole-design Y move that rounds them to one height (or apart) swaps their order, because the place across then decides. Ordinary editing makes such twins. For example, 1.4 '+= 0.2' stores 1.5999999999999999 beside a twin typed as 1.6 (§11.9: typed values are never cleaned). 'Rotate by' and placement do it too. The editor's default snapped move (§11.8, clean(x0 + k·0.05)) rounds them to one height on every step.

- A17's two exact copies, one an ulp higher, swap the copy kept on 2 of 8 Y moves.
- On the plausible set, 20,676 designs had one twin of each tied pair moved one ulp, then 4 random Y moves each. G moved on 857 designs (1,027 moves), by up to 0.0506 (#14520). 5 changed a played tier: C09 cylinder ribs #7864 and #7894 (Sharpening), laminated hilts #22569 and #22914 (Hammering), and fuller #24231.

summary:
The fix does what it set out to do on every corpus: whole-design Y, Z and random moves move no G or kept flag, and as built it changes only what it says it does. I'm passing it as false, because three major problems stand.

1. **Twin heights.** Both ranks still order by the raw height, so two twin parts whose heights differ in the last bit swap under a Y move. That changes G on 857 of 20,676 perturbed plausible designs, 5 a tier. Such twins come from plain editing, and the editor's snapped move triggers it on every step. This was already true on f7ac37d, but the SPEC now says Y moves keep every step to the bit. Fix, tried: place the height in RANK_Q from the grip point like x and z. That changes nothing as built and closes all of it.
2. **Hidden part steers the measure's reference.** A hidden Grip speck or buried Grip block chooses which Grip near copy the verdict keeps. That moves the measure's point, which the SPEC says no cleaned part can do, and flips P5's Hammering from Hard to Normal. On every 9th plausible design built that way, 85 of 3,598 move G and one changes tier; f7ac37d moves none.
3. **Ids regression.** Part ids now decide between parts whose places round to the same RANK_Q step. P5 plays Hard or Normal by ids alone. This needs typed sub-1e-9 positions.

A tried alternative fixes all three and also the new sensitivity to sub-visible grip moves (G moves on 13.4 % of every third plausible design for a 1e-9 grip move). It orders tied parts from their own middle instead of from the grip, with heights placed in RANK_Q. As built it moves 43 of 33,389 plausible designs by at most 0.0167, with no tier change and no measurable cost. Adopting it means re-blessing X02, its golden and three unit cases.

Minor: the grip-move sensitivity above is not named in the SPEC; 17 mutants survived the suite, each now caught by a tried pin; each guard's own typed-only boundary is unnamed; and T-PERF-01 fails only under load, on f7ac37d as well.
